TESTED through confirm-kind's REAL branch with stub gate CLIs: exit 0 with GENERIC is stopped at once, exit 0 with NGC_SERIAL is confirmed, and no JSON, not seen, a failed probe, or a changed gate never confirms. A LAUNCH record needs a CONFIRMED verdict for the same pid and plan. A launch json in root_monitor ba031c23's exact format passes all 9 checks. The relaunch rules were TESTED end to end on stub monitor/driver pairs. Phase route_a at launch is FORMAL from the driver bytes: the first stage started is 01_route_a.
- (6) TSR is the M-7 TRUNCATION_SHAPE_RESIDUAL flag record, 61bd8a83 from bytes now. It is EXISTS_NOT_ADOPTED and is not a launch input.

findings.title: 0709 states A143 D2 in the plural, but the kit lets the twin start after the seed serial's LAUNCH record alone
findings.evidence:
- 0709 reads: 'Identity pair (A143 D2): the serial S0 calls launch first. The twin follows when the gate admits it.'
- order-check (s0_kit L986-991) requires only a seed-serial LAUNCH record and the seed registry; j0-j2 are not checked. P5s-15 TESTED the seed requirement.
- Gate v003 refuses the twin while any S0 serial is in route A. P7-02: seed NGC_SERIAL in route A, fp 3.7 GB, d1 = 6.0+11.0+50.3+16.4 = 83.7 GB > 83.0 GB, MEMORY_HARD.
- It admits the twin once that serial has passed route A (P7-03: 71.3 GB).
- So the twin can start after the seed's route A and before j0-j2 launch. j0's admission then waits, at the same 83.7 GB sum, until the twin stops.
- If D2 means all four S0 serials first, the twin's order-check should also require the J LAUNCH records. The V006 A143 text is NGC3198-named and was not opened.
- No wrong spec, outdir or caps can result; the effect is ordering only.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: The M-15 record, and with it the V006 write freeze, starts at the first --launch attempt, before the order, fill, dry-plan, admission, External1, step-2 and watch checks
findings.evidence:
- The serial script writes the record at step 2 (L97-120).
- Then come order-check (L131-134), fill (L137-144), dry plan (L147-155), admission (L170-174), ext1/step2/watch (L186-189) and freeze-check (L192-194).
- freeze-check (s0_kit L997-1013) refuses V006_CHANGED_SINCE_RECORD while launches/ is empty.
- Root's record runs show both halves, ok in RESULTS 1b788d60 and d127aaee: L14 (admission refused, record already written) and L12 (V006 changed, freeze refuses).
- So a transient refusal leaves the freeze in force until the eventual launch, for example the A133 memory rule (footprint <= 53.79 GB) while the campaign runs.
- Any V006 write in between refuses the seed in that launch root for good. Recovery needs a fresh launch root and leaves an orphan record.
- Not class (a): A142 item 6 rules M-15 first, and an operator who keeps the freeze is never refused.
- Suggest the refusal text say the freeze is now in force, or, if A142 allows, write the record after the transient checks.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: The kit has no path for the A141 L1 OUTPUT_CAP rerun (output cap raised) or for the A133 3(c) cap reruns
findings.evidence:
- 0707 L1: an OUTPUT_CAP stop under 3(c) is rerun with the output cap raised.
- The caps are kit constants (s0_kit L69-70), checked against CAPS_S45_C2V003 35f66b6a (L325-328) and as exact strings in monitor-argv (L1067-1070). P3-50..52 TESTED: any other output cap is refused.
- A LAUNCH record of a name blocks every later attempt (order-check L957-959, register L588-589; P5l-08 TESTED).
- The relaunch path covers procedural mis-launches only.
- A rerun with a raised cap therefore needs a kit successor or a ruled manual path. That path should be ready before a 7-day S0 call can end in OUTPUT_CAP.
findings.label: FORMAL

findings.title: register's same-spec test compares the whole parsed V006 pin dicts, line numbers included, so an edit above the pin lines refuses an honest relaunch
findings.evidence:
- register (s0_kit L590-594) compares the old and new v006_spec_pin and v006_handoff_pin.
- These are parse_v006_pins dicts {kind, name, sha256, path, entry, line} (record writer L89).
- TESTED P8b-2: with the same spec bytes and one V006 line inserted above the pins (spec pin line 17 -> 18), register refuses with REGISTRY_ENTRY_EXISTS_FOR_ANOTHER_SPEC, exit 3.
- An appended entry is reused: ALREADY_REGISTERED_SAME_SPEC (P8b-3; root K05).
- So an edit above the pin lines between attempt 1 and a relaunch or retry refuses it, although the spec and its sha are unchanged.
- Keep V006 append-only during S0, or compare only sha256 and path.
findings.label: TESTED

findings.title: The twin kill watch never kills when it cannot read its inputs, but then exits silently, and the twin runs on to its 22,752 s wall cap
findings.evidence:
- TESTED P7w-08..11, with a corrupt launch json, a missing launch json, an unreadable stages dir and an unreadable twin spec: each exits 3 with the twin and the serial stub still alive.
- The watch writes only to work/.../kill_watch.out.txt (twin script L211). Nothing alerts root when the watch ends before the twin's receipt.
- A failing ps inside kill-target reads as CHILD_NOT_ALIVE (exit 1), and the watch then also exits 3 without killing.
- Step-5 L4 (review_step5_path_c3) showed that the pair memory window relies on this kill.
- Suggest an alert when the kill-watch process is gone while the twin is alive.
findings.label: TESTED

corrections: L1 arithmetic (FORMAL and TESTED on gate v003 code; class unchanged). A J serial's admission sum is 83.7 GB only after the seed serial has ended. While the seed is still alive after route A, the sum is 93.7 GB (10 + 11 + 6 + 50.3 + 16.4; probes E09 and E10). The J start also waits only until the twin leaves route A, which is earlier than 'until the twin stops'.

L1 context (TESTED on gate v003 code; still a NOTE). The plural reading of A143 D2, with all four S0 serials launched before the twin, conflicts with gate v003. twin_start_check refuses the twin on MEMORY_HARD while any S0 serial is in route A: d1 >= 6 + 11 + 50.3 + 16.4 = 83.7 GB > 83 GB (E01, E06). It refuses on MEMORY_KNEE while two or more serials are alive after route A: d2 = 10n + 61.3 GB > 72 GB for n >= 2 (E03 to E05). Under that reading the twin could start only after three of the four serials have ended. The kit's seed-only order lets the twin run after the seed's route A, and the J starts wait instead. Root should state which order D2 means.

L5 consequence (FORMAL and TESTED; still a NOTE). Under gate v003 and the kit's order, the twin can start only after the seed serial has left route A (E01, E02). While the twin is in route A, gate v003 refuses every S0 serial head on memory (E09, E10) and every DDO head on TWIN_HOLD. So a dead kill watch costs time: the twin runs on to its 22,752 s cap, and J and DDO starts wait. It does not cost memory safety. The Step-5 L4 pair-window argument came before the adopted twin_start_check. The alert suggestion stands.

L2 wording (FORMAL). The finding says a V006 write 'refuses the seed in that launch root for good'. That holds unless V006 is restored byte for byte, because freeze-check compares only the sha with the record's. In practice it is permanent, as stated.

Checked item (2) nuance (FORMAL; no effect). The record does bind attempt 1's outdir, receipt and launch-receipt strings (…_A1, which also carry the run root). After a mis-launch, the first confirmed launch writes …_A2, which differs from the record's strings. Nothing compares the two, and the on-time rule uses only the epoch.

root_monitor ba031c23 (FORMAL).
- Popen(cmd, start_new_session=True): the driver leads its own group, with the monitor as parent.
- The launch json is written right after Popen. utc uses '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'; command is [PY, -I, -B, driver, run, --spec, S, --outdir, O]; pins.spec is {path, sha256}; caps carry the wall cap as a float; child_pid is an int; retries_allowed is 0.
- launch-record's 9 checks all pass on that format (probe C06).
- The driver's stage subprocesses are not started in a new session (L1847), so the group kill reaches them.

Caps and paths (TESTED; probe B, 48/48).
- DRY validate refuses: a trailing '/'; '..', '.' and '//' inside; a leading '//'; a sibling root such as External10; a root two levels down; a relative root; non-NGC_ names, an ngc3198 name and a name with a space; runs_ext; attempts 0, 100, 01, ' 1' and 1.0. It accepts attempt 99.
- monitor-argv refuses: wall caps 610323, 610325, 610330, 610324.0 and 6.10324e5; RSS off by one byte; output 64 GiB, +1 byte and float forms; '=' forms; extra or swapped flags; an outdir other than the planned string or with a trailing '/'; a relative or non-normal spec; an upper-case sha; another interpreter, monitor or driver; a wrong receipt.
- CAPS_S45_C2V003: 610,324 s = 2 x 305,162 s, 32 GiB and 136 GiB for the serial calls; 22,752 s, 86 GiB and 32 GiB for the twin.

- order-check admits attempt 2 only when attempt 1 has exactly one MISLAUNCH record, written under the same M-15 sha and naming the planned outdir and receipt. It also waits until attempt 1's receipt exists.

- J calls and the twin need the seed's LAUNCH record; the twin also needs the seed registry entry.
- launch-record LAUNCH refuses a verdict for another pid, a non-CONFIRMED verdict, and another plan's verdict.
- L4 re-derived: one line inserted above the pins gives REGISTRY_ENTRY_EXISTS_FOR_ANOTHER_SPEC; an entry appended at the end reuses the registry entry. Root appends to V006 in practice (A150, A151).

New NOTE (TESTED, probe C31; not reachable on the honest path).
